title: Accessibility criteria catalog partition
description: A reviewed partition of the criteria catalog. Each entry records which evidence methods may decide a criterion. Coverage and EARL outcome both resolve adequacy through this data, so a permissive entry authorizes a conformance pass that no automated check can retract. Partitions are authored per framework so a reviewer approves a human-sized set.

catalogVersion.description: Date the partition was last reviewed. Rendered artifacts record this so a consumer can tell which adequacy rules produced a verdict.

framework.description: Framework this partition covers. Must match the framework recorded on probe results.

classification.description: Whether entries are external standards criteria or repository-internal quality checks. Internal checks are not conformance criteria and must not be presented as such.

source.description: Where the criterion definitions come from.

basis.description: Where the adequacy judgments come from.

reviewedBy.description: Qualified accessibility reviewer who approved these adequacy judgments. Null until reviewed. An agent never records itself here.

method.description: Must name a method defined in methods.json. An unknown method is rejected rather than silently ranked zero.

id.description: Criterion identifier as it appears on probe results.

level.description: Conformance level. Omitted for entries that are not standards criteria.

failureClass.description: Failure class from the skill's method-adequacy doctrine. Every class except static-decidable and internal requires an interaction probe or an assistive-technology pass to be decided rather than informed.

adequateMethods.description: Methods that may decide this criterion. Required even when empty, so an unreviewed omission cannot pass as a deliberate empty set. An empty list combined with humanJudgment records that no available method decides the criterion.

required.description: True when deciding the criterion depends on judging meaning, quality, or intent that no available method can evaluate.

reason.description: Why a person must decide. Stated plainly so a reviewer can check the judgment rather than infer it from an empty method list.

notes.description: Optional scope qualifier, for example which facet of a multi-part criterion a method can decide.
